features.title: Built different

inviteOnly.title: Invite-Only Access
inviteOnly.description: A space is reachable only by invite link — and by default the link isn't enough on its own: each person asks to join and you approve them. Switch on auto-approve and anyone holding the link walks straight in.

folders.title: Files or Whole Folders
folders.description: Share single files, or a whole folder that keeps itself in sync as you work. Others can browse it and take what they need, or mirror it to their own device as a live copy that follows every change.

noLimits.title: No Limits, No Meter
noLimits.description: Move a 500 GB master as easily as a PDF. No size caps and no per-GB bill — ever. Transfers pause and resume, pick themselves back up when the other person returns, and every finished file is checked against the original.

direct.title: Direct Device-to-Device
direct.description: Files move straight between devices over encrypted connections, served in place from the originals. No server stores your files, and anything that forwards traffic sees only ciphertext.

encrypted.title: Encrypted by Default
encrypted.description: Every connection between devices is end-to-end encrypted, with no keys to manage. On your device, Mirall encrypts its own records — which spaces you're in, who's in them, and what you share — and keeps your identity key in the system keychain, so a stolen laptop reveals none of it.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.description: Everything you need to know about Mirall.

items.question: Where are my files stored?
items.answer: On your device, and only your device — right where they already are. Sharing a file leaves it where it is on your disk; other members download it directly from you, and no server stores your files along the way. Once someone downloads a file, they have their own local copy.

items.question: Do both of us need to be online at the same time?
items.answer: Yes. Files move directly between devices, so the person sharing a file has to be online and running Mirall while you download it — there's no server holding a copy in the middle. You don't have to sit and watch it, though: if either of you drops off, the transfer pauses and picks up where it left off the next time you're both online.

items.question: Will Mirall work on my network?
items.answer: Almost always, and with no setup — Mirall finds its own way through home and office routers, so there are no ports to forward and nothing to configure. The exception is a network that blocks the traffic it needs to connect two devices directly, which some strict corporate firewalls, mobile routers and VPNs do. When that happens Mirall says so instead of leaving you guessing: it checks whether other people can actually reach you, names what's in the way, and lists what to try, in order. If that isn't enough, it can save a diagnostics file — with your identifying details left out — to send us.

items.question: What happens when I'm offline?
items.answer: Files you've already downloaded stay on your device — they're yours, and they work offline. Other members can still see what you've shared, but they can't download it from you until you're back. Downloading a file doesn't make you a second source for it either: the member who shared a file is the one who serves it, so while they're offline it's marked “Owner offline” and waits for them.

items.question: Is it really encrypted?
items.answer: Yes. Every connection between devices is end-to-end encrypted, so nobody can see your files or metadata in transit, and there's no central server that could be breached. On your own device, Mirall's records are encrypted at rest and your identity key is wrapped using your operating system's keychain, so copying Mirall's data folder gives up neither.

items.question: How do I invite someone to a space?
items.answer: A space gives you an invite link. Getting it to the other person is up to you — Mirall never sends it on your behalf, so pass it through a channel you trust, ideally an end-to-end encrypted messenger. Treat the link like a key: anyone holding it can ask to join, and it works until the expiry you chose. Approval is the backstop — by default you still let each person in yourself, so a link that gets forwarded doesn't quietly hand someone access.

items.question: What languages does Mirall support?
items.answer: Five: English, German, French, Spanish, and Italian. Mirall picks up your OS language on first launch, and you can switch at any time.

items.question: Are there file size limits?
items.answer: No. Mirall is built for the files that break everything else — hundreds of gigabytes, or a single file into the terabytes, transfer like any other. Content is streamed in chunks rather than uploaded as a whole, there are no size caps, and there's no per-GB bill. Speed depends on your network and the sender's upload bandwidth. File count is a different matter: a space holds up to 100 individual files, and a shared folder up to 5,000.

items.question: What happens if a large transfer is interrupted?
items.answer: It carries on where it stopped. Mirall verifies each chunk as it arrives and keeps a record of your progress, so a dropped connection, a closed laptop, or the sender going offline costs you the interruption — not the transfer. You can pause and resume by hand, and when a file finishes, Mirall confirms its contents match the sender's original exactly.

items.question: Is Mirall open source?
items.answer: Yes. Mirall is licensed under the AGPL-3.0 and the source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/ok/mirall-app). That's what makes the rest of this page checkable: you don't have to take our word for how your files are handled — you can read the code and see for yourself.

items.question: Is Mirall free?
items.answer: Mirall is free for personal use, and we plan to offer additional paid services in the future.

items.question: How do I keep Mirall up to date?
items.answer: You don't have to. Once installed, Mirall updates itself in the background and the new version is live the next time you launch — no reinstalls, no installer downloads.

problems.title: Common problems
problems.intro: A handful of things come up often enough to be worth naming. Each one is covered in full in the documentation.

items.symptom: On Windows, the installer says the app package can't be opened
items.check: The error comes from **App Installer**, the Windows component behind a double-clicked `.msix` — not from Mirall, and not from the part of Windows that does the installing. One PowerShell command installs it directly and skips App Installer entirely.
items.linkLabel: Install Mirall on Windows when the package won't open

items.symptom: Someone you invited is stuck on “Waiting to be let into…”
items.check: A member of the space has to be online and reachable before anyone can be let in. That includes **auto-approve**, which removes the approval step but not the hand-over — the link carries the address of the space, never the key to it.
items.linkLabel: Fix a join that gets stuck

items.symptom: Your avatar has a coloured ring, or a transfer won't start
items.check: Red means Mirall can't reach other people at all, amber that it can reach some but not others. The notification's **What can I do?** opens a page that names the likely cause and lists what to try, in order.

items.symptom: A file reads “Owner offline” and won't download
items.check: Files are served from the device that shared them, not from a server. The person who shared it has to be online and running Mirall while you download.
Nothing is lost. A transfer picks up where it stopped as soon as you're both back online, and you can pause and resume it by hand.
items.linkLabel: Pause, resume, cancel, or retry a transfer

items.check: Every link carries an expiry — 2 hours, 2 days, or 2 weeks. Once it lapses Mirall turns it down, and you need a fresh one.

items.symptom: Downloads fail because the download folder is unavailable
items.check: Mirall can't reach the folder it saves into — usually an external drive or a network share that went away. Reconnect it, or choose another folder.

report.title: Before you report a problem
report.intro: Anything you can tell us here saves a round trip. Most reports come down to what each device could see at the time.
items: **What you did, and what happened instead.** The exact wording Mirall showed you is worth copying out.
**Whether both devices were running Mirall** at the moment it went wrong.
**What Profile → This device → Connection says** — the headline, and the Connection summary underneath it.
**Which version each device is running.** Yours is on the Profile page, under **App**.
report.consoleIntro: For anything connection-related, the most useful thing you can attach is Mirall's own view of the network. Open **Profile → This device → Connection**, scroll to **Diagnostics**, and click **Save diagnostics**. Leave **Remove identifying details** switched on — your IP address, keys and space names are shortened or left out, and it is still enough for us to work from. **Preview what's included** shows you exactly what the file holds before you save it.
report.consoleNote: The file describes how your network behaves — not what you share or who you share it with. If we ask you for **Include detailed logs**, switch it on, reproduce the problem, and save the file afterwards.

tutorials.label: Tutorials
tutorials.heading: Tutorials
tutorials.intro: Guided lessons for newcomers. Follow them top to bottom — each one takes you all the way through a real task so you learn Mirall by doing.

items.title: Send your first files
items.intro: In a few minutes you'll install Mirall, create a space, invite someone, approve them, and watch a file travel directly from your device to theirs. You only need a second person with Mirall installed to receive — or a second computer of your own.

items.title: Install and open Mirall
items.text: Download Mirall for your platform from the download page and open it. The first time it launches, Mirall asks for a **display name** and an optional **avatar** — that's how other members will see you. Your OS language is detected automatically.

items.title: Create a space
items.text: On the **Shared Spaces** screen, click **Create Space**, give it a name, pick an icon, and click **Initialize Space**. Mirall confirms with **Space Created** — click **Done**. A space is a private group where you and the people you approve share files.

items.title: Create an invite link
items.text: Open the space and click **Invite**. Choose whether to **auto-approve** anyone who uses the link, pick how long it stays valid — **2 hours**, **2 days**, or **2 weeks** — and click **Create invite link**. Copy the link and send it however you like: chat, email, anything.

items.title: Let them join
items.text: The other person clicks **Join Space**, pastes the link, and confirms. Unless you turned auto-approve on, they now wait: their screen reads **Waiting to be let into** the space, and they can't see anything shared in the space yet.

items.title: Approve them
items.text: Back in your space, a banner appears reading **“<name> wants to join”**. Click **Approve**. They're admitted, the space contents open up to them, and you both appear in each other's **Members** panel.

items.title: Share a file
items.text: Drag a file onto the **Drop to Share** zone in the sidebar, or use **Share…** to pick one. Mirall offers it to the space straight from the original on your disk — it never makes a second copy.

items.title: Download on the other side
items.text: On the other person's Mirall, the file appears with a download button. They click it and the file transfers directly from your device to theirs, with live progress, speed, and time remaining. When it lands, a green shield confirms the contents match your original exactly. No server stored a copy along the way.

blocks.alt: Mirall's welcome screen asking for a display name and an optional avatar before first use
Mirall's Invite to Space dialog with an auto-approve toggle and a link expiry choice of 2 hours, 2 days, or 2 weeks
A Mirall space showing a “wants to join” banner with Approve and Deny buttons above the shared files
A Mirall space with shared files, the Drop to Share zone, and the Members panel in the sidebar

blocks.text: Nothing downloads automatically. Members always see what's available and choose what to pull onto their own device.

items.title: Share a folder and keep it in sync
items.intro: Instead of picking files one by one, you can share a whole folder into a space and keep it in sync. This lesson walks you through sharing a folder, then having another member mirror it to their own disk.

items.title: Open a space
items.text: Open an existing space, or create one as in the first tutorial. Anything you share lives inside a space.

items.title: Add a folder
items.text: Open **Add Folder** (from **Share…** in the sidebar, the **File** menu, or `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + U`). Pick a folder on your computer and give it a **share name** — that's how the folder appears to other members. Subfolders are included automatically.

items.title: Check the preview
items.text: Click **Next: Preview**. Mirall scans the folder in the background and shows you what it's about to share — how many files and how large. Click **Add Folder** to confirm.

items.title: Watch it publish
items.text: Mirall starts offering the folder's files to the space, serving them straight from the originals on your disk. From now on, when you add, edit, or remove files in that folder on your computer, the change syncs to the space on its own.

items.title: Have a member mirror it
items.text: Another member opens the shared folder. They can **browse** it — open subfolders and download individual files — or use **Mirror to Disk…** to keep a live, always-up-to-date copy in a folder of their choosing.

items.title: Watch it stay in sync
items.text: Change a file in your shared folder. On the mirroring member's computer, the mirror updates to match. The mirror is **read-only**: if they edit a mirrored file, it's restored to your version on the next sync.

blocks.alt: Mirall's Add Folder dialog with a folder path, a share name field, and a Next: Preview button
A Mirall space with a shared Production Footage folder card marked “Shared by you”

blocks.text: Sharing a folder never doubles its disk usage — Mirall serves the files in place, from the originals.

guides.label: How-to guides
guides.heading: How-to guides
guides.intro: Task-focused recipes. Each one assumes you already know the basics and gets you straight to a single goal.

items.text: Click **Create Space** on the Shared Spaces screen.
Give the space a name and pick an icon.
Click **Initialize Space**. Mirall confirms with **Space Created**.
Click **Done**. You now have a space to yourself — invite people from inside it.

blocks.text: Creating a space doesn't hand you an invite. Open the space and use **Invite** when you're ready to add someone.

items.text: Click **Join Space** on the Shared Spaces screen.
Paste the invite link you received. Both the `mirall://join/…` link and the bare code work.
Optionally give the space a local name — only you will see it.
Click **Join Space**.

blocks.text: Unless the invite was set to auto-approve, joining is a **request**: your screen reads **Waiting to be let into** the space until an existing member approves you. You can leave the window open — you'll be admitted automatically as soon as a member is online, and you don't need to be online at the moment they approve. Until then the space's contents stay closed to you, and the only action available is **Cancel request**.

Once someone approves you, the space opens and its files appear. If the invite had **auto-approve** turned on, nobody has to decide — you are let in as soon as your device reaches a member of the space.
An invite link has an expiry. If yours has lapsed, Mirall tells you the link has expired — ask the person who sent it for a new one.

image.alt: Mirall showing it is waiting to be let into a space, with the existing members' avatars and a Cancel request button

related.label: Fix a join that gets stuck

blocks.text: Open the space and click **Invite**. The dialog asks you two things before it mints a link:

items: **Auto-approve** — off by default. Leave it off and everyone who uses the link asks to join, and you approve each one. Turn it on and nobody has to approve: anyone holding the link is let in as soon as their device reaches a member of the space.
**Link expires after** — **2 hours**, **2 days**, or **2 weeks**. After that the link stops working and Mirall refuses anyone who tries to use it.

blocks.text: Click **Create invite link**. Mirall shows a single `mirall://join/…` link, tagged with the choices you made, and a **Copy** button. Send it however you like — chat, email, anything. The same link works for as many people as you want to admit, until it expires. **Change** takes you back to adjust the settings; **Done** closes the dialog.

The link carries the space name, so the person joining sees what they're joining. It does not carry the key to the space — that is handed over by a device that is already a member, so someone has to be online and reachable when the link is used, auto-approve or not.

image.alt: Mirall's Invite to Space dialog with an auto-approve toggle and a link expiry choice of 2 hours, 2 days, or 2 weeks

docs.title: Approve or deny join requests
docs.intro: When someone uses an invite that isn't set to auto-approve, they stay outside the space until a member lets them in. Any member can do this — not just whoever created the space.

blocks.text: A banner appears at the top of the space reading **“<name> wants to join”**, with **Approve** and **Deny** beside it. Approving hands them the key to the space's contents; denying turns them away.

When several people are waiting, the banner collapses into a stack of avatars and a count — **“3 people want to join”** — with a **Review** button. That opens **Requests to join**, where you can tick individuals and **Approve selected**, take everyone at once with **Approve all**, or deny someone from their row.

Requests reach you in three places: the banner inside the space, a notice in the app with a **Review** button that takes you there, and a **“1 waiting”** pill on that space's tile in the Shared Spaces overview. The notice only appears while Mirall's window is open — there is no desktop notification for join requests, so one that arrives while the window is closed waits for you inside the space.
A request only needs handling once. As soon as any member approves or denies someone, the banner clears for everyone else in the space.

image.alt: Mirall's “Requests to join” dialog listing people waiting to join, with Approve selected and Approve all buttons

related.label: Fix a join that gets stuck

docs.title: Fix a join that gets stuck
docs.intro: Someone follows your invite link, their screen reads **Waiting to be let into** the space, and nothing appears on yours. That almost always means the request never reached a member's device — not that you missed a button.

items.title: Check both devices are running Mirall
items.text: A join request travels straight from one device to the other, so a member of the space has to be online and running Mirall at the moment the link is used. A closed app or a sleeping laptop on your side is enough to stall it. Running in the background counts — Mirall in the menu bar or the notification area is reachable.

items.title: Look where the request actually appears
items.text: The banner is **inside the space**. From the Shared Spaces overview all you get is a **“1 waiting”** pill on that space's tile. Mirall also raises a notice with a **Review** button, but only while the window is open — there is no desktop notification for join requests.

items.title: Check your own connection
items.text: Open your **Profile** page and click **Connection**. If the headline reads **Connecting to the Mirall network…** rather than **Network is healthy**, nothing can reach you yet. Open **Show advanced details** and read the **Suggestions** underneath — that is where **“Your router appears to be blocking inbound UDP”** and the warnings about your network type appear.

items.title: Rule out a firewall or a VPN
items.text: Mirall connects over UDP, and a VPN, a company network, or a firewall that blocks it will stop two devices finding each other. On Windows, open **Windows Security → Firewall & network protection → Allow an app through firewall** and check that Mirall is ticked for both **Private** and **Public** — the prompt shown on first launch is easy to dismiss by accident. If you are on a VPN, try again with it off. Sharing a phone's connection has the same effect: both devices end up behind the carrier's network, where a direct connection often cannot be made.

items.title: Leave both apps running
items.text: A device that is waiting keeps knocking on its own, so once you are reachable the request arrives without anyone having to paste the link again.

blocks.text: **Auto-approve** changes none of this. It removes the decision, not the hand-over: the link carries the address of the space, never the key to it, so a device that is already a member still has to be reachable to let someone in. Until one is, the person joining waits exactly as they would without it.

Open the space, open the **More** menu, and choose **Add to Favorites**. Back on the Shared Spaces screen you can then filter the list by **All Spaces** or **Favorites**. Once a space is pinned, the same menu entry reads **Remove from Favorites**.

Open the space, open the **More** menu, and choose **Leave Space**. Mirall cancels any in-flight transfers and drops the space's records from your device. Files you've already downloaded, and any folder you were mirroring, stay where they are — they're yours.
If you're waiting to be approved rather than already a member, the same button reads **Cancel request** and simply withdraws your request.

docs.title: Replace a space marked Unsupported
docs.intro: A space made by a much older version of Mirall carries a red **Unsupported** badge beside its name and a banner saying it can no longer be used. It can't be converted, so move what you need into a new space.

blocks.text: The space stays visible and you can still read what it holds, but the parts that would change it are closed off: **Invite** and **Edit Space** are greyed out, and the **Drop to Share** zone is gone, so nothing new can be shared into it.

items.text: Create a new space from the Shared Spaces screen.
Invite the same people to it, and approve them as they ask to join.
Share your folders and files into the new space.
When everyone has moved across, open the old space's **More** menu and choose **Leave Space**.

blocks.text: **Manage Storage** still works on an unsupported space, so you can see what it takes up and reclaim it before you go. Anything you already downloaded from it is an ordinary file on your disk and stays there after you leave.

Drag files onto the **Drop to Share** zone in the sidebar, or use **Share…** to pick them from your computer. While you drag a file over the space, the drop zone grows to fill the whole area, so you don't have to aim carefully. Mirall offers the file to the space right away.
Mirall shares the file **in place**, straight from the original on your disk. Sharing never doubles a file's disk usage, and when you edit a shared file, the change is picked up where it lies.

There's no size limit. Hundreds of gigabytes, or a file into the terabytes, all work the same way — content is streamed in chunks rather than uploaded as a whole. Mirall does need a moment to index a file before sharing can start, so expect a short **Preparing** step on something that large. Members waiting on it can watch that preparation progress rather than staring at a blank spinner.
Want to share a whole folder instead of picking files? See **Share a whole folder**.

Click the download button on any file shared by another member. The file transfers directly from their device to yours, showing live progress, average speed, and an estimate of the time remaining. Downloads land in your chosen download folder.
When a download finishes, a green shield appears next to the file. That's Mirall confirming the contents it received match the owner's original exactly.

docs.title: Pause, resume, cancel, or retry a transfer

blocks.text: If your network drops or the member you're downloading from goes offline, the transfer pauses on its own and picks back up from where it left off once that person is back. A member who has set an upload limit is a different case — they are still there, just sending slowly — so the transfer waits its turn instead of failing, and an interrupted download keeps retrying on its own for as long as it makes progress. You can also take control by hand — the buttons on a file row change with its state:

items: **Pause Download** — stop a running download. Its progress is kept, so resuming costs you nothing.
**Cancel** — stop a running download outright and throw away what's been received.
**Resume** — continue a paused download from where it stopped.
**Discard Partial** — throw away a download that's paused or stalled and free the space it was using.
**Retry** — reattempt a download that ended in an error; **Dismiss** clears the failed row instead.

blocks.text: In-progress downloads are written to a `.mirall.part` file and renamed to their real name only when the transfer completes — an interrupted transfer can't leave a half-written file under its final name.
A mirrored folder has no per-file download controls. To pause or stop everything a folder is pulling, use the mirror's own **Pause Mirror**, **Resume Mirror**, and **Unmount Mirror** actions.

related.label: Pause, resume, move, or stop a mirror

docs.title: See who's downloading from you
docs.intro: For any file you share, Mirall shows you who is pulling it right now.

blocks.text: While someone downloads a file you've shared, their avatar appears on that file's row, along with a combined progress bar, the transfer speed, and an estimate of the time remaining. If several people are downloading at once, their avatars stack up with a count.

Click the row's indicator to expand it. You'll see each person individually — their name, how far along they are, their own speed, and their own time remaining. Someone who has paused shows as **Paused**; someone who has dropped offline mid-transfer shows as **Waiting**.
This works for loose files in a space and for files inside a folder you share. It only appears on files you own — you don't see other people's downloads from other people.

image.alt: A shared file in Mirall expanded to show each person downloading it, with their avatar, progress, speed, and time remaining

blocks.text: Use a file's menu and choose **Unshare from Space** to remove a file you added so it's no longer offered to other members. Files they've already downloaded stay on their devices — unsharing only stops offering new copies. Your own original is untouched.

docs.title: Share a whole folder
docs.intro: Share a folder into a space and Mirall keeps it in sync — add, edit, or remove files and everyone in the space sees the change automatically. Subfolders come along too.

items.text: Open the space you want to share into.
Open **Add Folder** from **Share…** in the sidebar, the **File** menu, or `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + U`.
Choose a folder on your computer with **Browse…** and give it a **share name** — how it appears to other members. The name must be unique within the space.
Click **Next: Preview**. Mirall scans the folder and shows what it's about to share — the file count and total size.
Click **Add Folder**. Mirall starts offering the folder's files. Changes you make to the folder later sync to the space automatically.

blocks.text: Folders you share are marked **Shared by you**. Mirall serves the files straight from the originals, so sharing a folder never doubles its disk usage.

image.alt: Mirall's Add Folder dialog with a folder path, a share name field, and a Next: Preview button

related.label: Pause or stop adding a folder

docs.title: Pause or stop adding a folder
docs.intro: Mirall reads through a folder you share before it can offer the contents to anyone. While that's under way the folder tells you how much is left, and lets you hold it or clear it.

items.text: Open the folder from its card in the space.
A notice above the file list reads **Adding 6 files to this folder**, followed by how much there is left to read. Before the count is known it reads **Looking for files to add…**.
Click **Pause** to hold the queue where it is. The notice turns amber and reads **Adding files is paused**, and the folder's card in the space is badged **Paused**.
Click **Resume** to carry on from where it stopped.

blocks.alt: A folder shared in Mirall with a notice reading “Adding 6 files to this folder · 805.3 MB to read” and Pause and Stop buttons

blocks.text: Pause and Stop are not the same

items: **Pause** is remembered. The folder stays paused until you resume it — quitting Mirall and starting it again leaves it paused.
**Stop** clears what's queued without recording a pause, so there's nothing to resume. Mirall picks the folder up again on its own the next time it looks over what you share.

blocks.alt: A paused folder in Mirall, with an amber notice reading “Adding files is paused. Resume to finish adding this folder.” and a Resume button

blocks.text: Neither one unshares the folder, and neither withdraws the files already added — those stay available to the space. Only a folder you share carries these controls: open a folder someone else shares and the same notice tells you what the owner is still adding, with nothing for you to act on.
Open a folder another member shared to see what's inside without downloading everything. A folder you're only looking through is marked **Browse**.

Subfolders are rows you can open and close. Each one tells you what's inside before you open it: how many files it holds and their total size, how many are already on your device, how many are downloading right now, and how many subfolders it contains. **Expand all** opens the whole tree at once, and flips to **Collapse all** to fold it back up.

If the owner is still working through the folder, a notice above the list says so — **Michael is adding 6 files to this folder**, with how much is left to read. Those files appear as the owner gets to them, so a folder can keep growing while you look at it.
Click **Download** on any individual file to save just that one, or use **Mirror to Disk…** to keep the whole folder synced instead.
Folders you leave open stay open as you move around the app. Restarting Mirall resets the tree to its default, with the top-level folders open.

image.alt: A shared folder in Mirall browsed as a tree, with subfolders showing file counts and sizes and an Expand all button

docs.title: Mirror a folder to disk
docs.intro: Keep a live, always-up-to-date copy of a shared folder in a folder on your own computer.

items.text: Open the shared folder and choose **Mirror to Disk…**.
Pick a location on your computer with **Browse…**, then click **Next: Preview** to see what will be downloaded.
Click **Start Mirroring**. Mirall downloads the contents and keeps them in sync as the owner makes changes.

blocks.text: A mirror is **read-only**. If you edit a file inside the mirror, Mirall restores it to the owner's version on the next sync. To keep your own edits, copy the file out of the mirror folder first.

A mirror can't be placed directly on a top-level personal folder such as Home, Desktop, Documents, or Downloads. If the mirror's folder already holds a file of your own with the same name as a shared one, your file is left alone and the mirrored copy lands under a different name.

image.alt: Mirall's Mirror to Disk dialog, picking a location for a read-only copy that stays in sync with the owner's folder

docs.title: Pause, resume, move, or stop a mirror

items: **Pause Mirror** — stop syncing for now; the folder stays where it is and won't update until you resume.
**Resume Mirror** — start syncing again from wherever the owner's copy is now.
**Change Mirror Location…** — move the mirror to a different folder on your computer. This one lives on the folder's card in the space view.
**Unmount Mirror** — stop mirroring entirely and remove the mirrored copy. The folder reverts to **Browse**.

blocks.text: If a write fails — a full disk, or a destination that's become read-only — the mirror pauses rather than erroring, and resumes once there's room.

image.alt: A mirrored folder in Mirall with every file marked “On your device” and confirmed by a green verified shield

docs.title: See who's mirroring a folder you shared
docs.intro: A folder you own shows you the people keeping a live copy of it.

blocks.text: Open a folder you share and look for **Mirrored by** in the sidebar. One person shows by name with their current state underneath. Several stack into a row of avatars with a summary beneath — for example **“2 Syncing… · 1 Synced”**.

Each person is in one of three states: **Synced** (their copy matches yours), **Syncing…** (they're still catching up), or **Paused** (they've paused their mirror). The states stay accurate even while those people are offline.

image.alt: The Mirrored by panel on a shared folder in Mirall, showing the people keeping a live copy and whether each is synced, syncing, or paused

blocks.text: Open **Settings → Storage**. The **Download Folder** section at the top shows where downloads land; **Change…** opens your OS picker. This is the folder every space uses unless it has one of its own, and the choice persists across restarts. It defaults to your OS Downloads folder.

Not every folder can be used. If the one you pick sits inside — or contains — a folder you share or mirror, Mirall refuses it, because anything downloaded there would be published to your peers. A folder that doesn't exist, or that Mirall can't write to, is refused too. Mirall never creates the folder for you.

Mirall keeps checking that the folder is still reachable. If it goes away — an ejected drive, a network share that dropped, a folder you deleted or renamed — a warning appears here and downloads stop rather than failing one by one.
Changing this folder doesn't move files you've already downloaded, and it leaves spaces that have set their own download folder alone.

related.label: Give one space its own download folder
Fix a download folder Mirall can't reach

docs.title: Give one space its own download folder
docs.intro: A space can save its downloads somewhere other than your default — a scratch disk for the project you're cutting, say, while everything else lands in Downloads.

items.text: Open the space, click **More** in the header, and choose **Edit Space**.
Under **Download Folder**, click **Change…** and pick a folder.
Click **Save Changes**. Closing the dialog without saving discards the change.

blocks.text: A space you leave alone keeps using the folder from **Settings → Storage**, and the dialog says so: **Using the default download folder**. Once a space has its own, a **Use default folder** button appears to put it back.

The same rule applies as for the default folder: a folder that sits inside — or contains — a folder you share or mirror is refused, since anything landing there would be published to your peers. Two spaces may happily share one folder.

Files you already downloaded are never moved. Ones now outside the space's folder simply read as **Available** again — point the space back at the old folder and they return to **On your device** without downloading anything twice. Let transfers finish or pause them before you switch.

image.alt: Mirall's Edit Space dialog showing the Download Folder section with a Change button and a note that the space is using the default download folder

docs.title: See how much disk space Mirall uses

blocks.text: Open **Settings → Storage** and look at **App Storage**. This is what Mirall itself occupies on your device — not your files. Because Mirall shares your files in place, it never keeps a second copy of them, so this figure stays small.
**Show details** breaks it into two parts:

items: **Shared-file index** — compact maps of the files you share, never their contents. Freed automatically when you stop sharing a file.
**App database** — your spaces, members, and sync history.

image.alt: Mirall's Storage settings showing the download folder and the App Storage breakdown into a shared-file index and app database

blocks.text: Mirall tidies up after itself as it goes, but you can prompt it. In **Settings → Storage**, open **Show details** under App Storage and click **Free up space**. Mirall compacts its own bookkeeping and reports how much it recovered — or tells you storage is already optimized.
This only touches Mirall's own data. Your shared files, your downloads, and your mirrored folders are never removed.

docs.title: Fix a download folder Mirall can't reach
docs.intro: An ejected external drive, a network share that dropped, or a folder that was deleted or renamed leaves Mirall with nowhere to put a download.

blocks.text: Rather than failing each download with a generic error, Mirall names the folder as the problem. A notification stays up for as long as the folder is unreachable and carries a **Change folder** action, and **Settings → Storage** shows the same warning under the download folder.

Reconnect the drive or remount the share and the warning clears on its own. If the folder is gone for good, use **Change folder** on the notification — or **Change…** in **Settings → Storage** — and pick another one.
Downloads heading for a folder that isn't there stop retrying instead of hammering it, and Mirall never quietly recreates a folder you deleted. Start them again once the folder is back.
A space with its own download folder is checked the same way, so the warning can name a folder other than the one in **Settings → Storage**.

related.label: Give one space its own download folder

blocks.text: Click your avatar in the top-right to open the **Profile** page. The card at the top holds your display name and picture — change either, then click **Save Changes**, which appears once there's something to save. The update propagates to every space you're in. Your profile is only shared with the peers you connect with, and a picture must be under 16 MB.

docs.title: Check how your identity is protected

blocks.text: Your identity in Mirall is a signing key held on your device. The **Identity protection** row under **This device** on your **Profile** page tells you how that key is being kept safe:

items: **Your identity key is protected by the system keychain** — the normal case. The key is wrapped using your operating system's secure keychain, so copying Mirall's data folder doesn't hand anyone your identity.
**No system keychain is available** — Mirall couldn't reach a keychain on this machine, so your identity key relies on full-disk encryption instead. Turning that on is worth doing here.
**Identity-key protection is disabled** — protection isn't active on this install.

blocks.text: This row is information, not a button — there's nothing to click and nothing to configure.

docs.title: Fix a connection problem
docs.intro: Mirall judges whether other people can actually reach this device, not just whether you have internet — so it can tell you your network is the problem instead of leaving you to guess.

blocks.text: Your avatar gains a soft pulsing ring when something is wrong — red when Mirall can't reach other people at all, amber when it can reach some but not others. No ring means you're connected and ready.

A problem also raises a notification that stays up until it clears. Its **What can I do?** action opens the **Connection problem** page. You land on that page directly if you open Mirall with no spaces yet and a connection that isn't working.
The Connection problem page
It opens with a verdict in plain language and what that means for you:

items: **Your network is blocking Mirall** — Mirall can find other people but can't connect to any of them. Invites you send won't arrive and spaces you join won't sync.
**Limited connection** — connections to many people will fail, though sharing still works with some. A mobile router or phone tethering is the usual cause.
**You're offline** — this device isn't connected to any network at all.
**Can't reach the network** — every route out of this device goes through a VPN, and nothing is answering through it.

blocks.text: Under **What helps, in this order**, Mirall lists numbered steps picked for the problem it actually found. Turning a VPN off comes first when the VPN is the likely culprit; when your network hands out a different port every time, it says so plainly, because no router setting fixes that one.

**Check again** re-runs the test on the spot instead of waiting for the next automatic one, with the time of the last check beside it. **Network details** opens the full diagnostics, and **Connection history** opens your activity log filtered to connection events. **Continue to Spaces** takes you on — you can still create and join spaces, and they start syncing once the connection works.
Things worth checking

items: **A VPN.** Many route or block the traffic Mirall needs. Try again with it off.

**Your firewall.** On Windows, open **Windows Security → Firewall & network protection → Allow an app through firewall** and check that Mirall is ticked for both **Private** and **Public**. The prompt shown on first launch is easy to dismiss by accident.
**A company or campus network.** Strict networks often block a direct connection between two devices outright.
**A phone's shared connection.** Tethering puts both devices behind the carrier's network, where a direct connection frequently cannot be made.

blocks.text: **Settings → Network** is a different screen — it sets bandwidth limits and shows no connection status. The diagnostics live on **Network status**, which you reach from **Profile → This device → Connection**.

related.label: Why Mirall can tell your network is the problem
Fix a join that gets stuck

docs.title: Send us a diagnostics file
docs.intro: When a connection problem is hard to put into words, Mirall can write down what it sees about your network so you don't have to.

items.text: Open **Profile → This device → Connection** to reach **Network status**.
Scroll to **Diagnostics**. Leave **Remove identifying details** switched on — it is the recommended setting, and it is enough for us to work from.
Click **Preview what's included** if you'd like to read the file first. It shows exactly what will be saved.
Click **Save diagnostics**, then attach the file to your message.

blocks.text: The file describes how your network behaves — not what you share or who you share it with. With **Remove identifying details** on, your IP address, keys and space names are shortened or left out.

**Include detailed logs** is for a problem we can't reproduce. Switching it on turns detailed logging on straight away, so reproduce the problem first and save the file afterwards — otherwise the lines we need are the ones that were never recorded.
Turning **Remove identifying details** off saves the same file with nothing withheld, and the preview says so in as many words. Only do that if we've asked you to.

docs.title: Review what happened in your spaces
docs.intro: Mirall keeps a record on your device of who joined, left, or was approved, what was shared and downloaded, and when this device's connection went wrong.

blocks.text: Click your avatar to open **Profile**, then choose **Activity Log** under **This device**. The row itself tells you how many events are recorded.

Search across people, files and folders with the box at the top, and narrow the list with three menus — **All spaces**, **Anyone**, and **Any time** (last 7, 30, or 90 days). The **All / Members / Files / Folders / Security / Network** buttons filter by kind, and you can press more than one. Every filter you apply becomes a chip you can remove individually, or clear in one go with **Clear all**. Press **⌘F** (**Ctrl-F**) to jump to the search box.

Events are grouped by day, newest first, with your own actions attributed to **You**. A refused request or a failed transfer carries a **DENIED** or **FAILED** badge. Twenty events load at a time — **Load more** fetches the next page.
Connection history

**Network** is the log's account of the stretches when nothing could happen. It records when this device went offline, when Mirall couldn't reach anyone, and when a connection was restored, along with members dropping out and coming back. A restored entry carries how long the gap lasted — **Offline for 20m** — and names the cause it settled on, such as **Your VPN is the only route out** or **Your router changes ports**.

That's what turns an unexplained quiet afternoon into a window you can point at. **Connection history** on the Connection problem and Network status screens opens the log already filtered this way. If nothing is there, Mirall says so: **No connection problems recorded**.
Spaces you have left still appear here, and stay filterable, until their events age out.

image.alt: Mirall's Activity Log listing recent events — files shared and downloaded, a folder mirrored, and members joining and leaving — with a search box and space, person and date filters above

related.label: What the activity log can tell you

blocks.text: Open **Settings → Activity Log**. **Record activity** turns recording on and off — it's on to begin with, and it covers connection problems as well as what happens in your spaces. Turning it off stops new events being written; it doesn't delete anything already recorded, and those events stay searchable and exportable.
**Keep events for** sets how long they're retained — **30 days**, **90 days**, or **365 days**, with 90 the starting point. Anything older is deleted automatically.

**Export as JSON** saves every recorded event to a file called `mirall-activity-log.json`, including the stretches when this device was offline. **Delete the log** removes them all and asks you to confirm first; it can't be undone. Deleting hands back the disk space the events were using, and keeps your retention setting.
An export contains raw identifiers — public keys, file paths, and content hashes — rather than the readable sentences you see in the app. Treat the file as sensitive.

related.label: Review what happened in your spaces

docs.title: Get around with the keyboard
docs.intro: Every screen in Mirall is reachable without the mouse. The ones you go to most often have a chord of their own; the rest live in the command palette.

blocks.text: Press **⌘K** (**Ctrl-K** on Windows and Linux) to open the command palette, then start typing. It searches your spaces by name and every action Mirall can run — including the screens with no shortcut of their own: **Network status**, each of the Settings pages, **What's new**, **Send feedback**, and the documentation.
**⌘/** (**Ctrl-/**) shows the full list of shortcuts inside the app at any time.

**⌘1** to **⌘9** jump straight to the first nine spaces in your list. On macOS that chord lives in the **View → Go to Space** menu, which is also where you can see which number belongs to which space.

Actions that act on a space — **Invite**, **Edit Space**, **Add to Favorites**, **Manage storage** — appear in the palette only while a space is open, and stay hidden while you're still waiting to be approved into one. Leaving is the exception: it stays available while you wait, because withdrawing the request is the thing you might want to do.
Shortcuts keep out of your way while you're typing: only **⌘K**, **⌘,**, **⌘/** and **⌘F** stay live inside a text field.

Mirall lives in your menu bar (macOS) or system tray (Windows and Linux). Closing the window keeps the app running so peers stay connected, transfers keep going, and notifications still arrive — click the icon to bring the window back.
**Settings → General** lets you opt out: **Show Mirall in the menu bar** on macOS, **Run in the background** on Windows and Linux. **Launch at login** starts Mirall quietly with your computer.
To quit Mirall outright rather than close it to the tray, use **File → Quit Mirall** (`Ctrl + Q`) on Windows and Linux, or **Mirall → Quit** (`Cmd + Q`) on macOS.

Mirall ships in five languages — English, German, French, Spanish, and Italian. Your OS locale is detected on first launch. Switch any time under **Settings → Appearance → Language**; your choice persists across restarts.

docs.title: Change the theme and display size

blocks.text: Under **Settings → Appearance**, pick a **Theme Mode** — Light, System, or Dark (System follows your OS automatically). Set the **Display Size** to Compact, Cozy, Default, or Spacious, or step through any zoom level with `Cmd/Ctrl +`, `−`, and `0`. Your choice persists across restarts.
On Windows and Linux, **Auto-hide the menu bar** tucks the menu bar away until you press `Alt`. Keyboard shortcuts keep working either way.

Mirall surfaces incoming files and space activity through your operating system's notification center. Open **Settings → Notifications**. Three switches cover the basics: **Show desktop notifications** (the master switch), **Play sound**, and **Mute when Mirall is focused**, which skips alerts while the window is in front.
Under **Events**, five per-event toggles let you opt in or out individually:

items: **Someone comes online** — a member of one of your spaces appears online.
**Someone goes offline** — a member of one of your spaces disconnects.
**Download finished** — a file you're receiving has finished downloading.
**Download failed** — a download could not be completed.
**Download paused** — a download paused because the sender went offline.

blocks.text: Requests to join a space always surface in the app itself, as a banner on the space and a notice you can act on. They don't depend on these settings.

docs.title: Limit how much bandwidth Mirall uses
docs.intro: Cap how fast Mirall transfers files, so a big download doesn't take the whole line with it.

blocks.text: Open **Settings → Network**. Under **Transfer limits** there's a row for **Download** and one for **Upload**, each offering **Unlimited**, **1 MB/s**, **5 MB/s**, **25 MB/s**, or **Custom**. Both start out unlimited.

**Custom** reveals a box where you type a figure in kilobytes per second — a plain number, no units to pick. Enter `0` for no limit. Anything below 32 KB/s is rounded up to it, and Mirall tells you so.
A change takes hold within a moment, including on transfers already running. There's nothing to restart and nothing to reconnect.

A limit is a **total, not a figure per transfer**. Two downloads running under a 5 MB/s cap get roughly half each rather than 5 MB/s apiece, and serving several people at once splits one upload cap between them.

image.alt: Mirall's Network settings showing Transfer limits, with separate Download and Upload rows offering Unlimited, 1 MB/s, 5 MB/s, 25 MB/s, or a custom figure

docs.title: Install Mirall on Windows when the package won't open
docs.intro: Double-clicking the `.msix` hands it to App Installer, a Windows component that can refuse a package the rest of Windows installs without complaint. When that happens, install it directly instead.

blocks.text: Use a **normal** PowerShell window. **Do not** run it as administrator — the command installs for the current user, so an elevated window puts Mirall on the administrator account and it never appears in your Start menu.

items.title: Download the installer
items.text: Get `Mirall.msix` from the download page and note where your browser saved it — normally your **Downloads** folder.

items.title: Open PowerShell
items.text: Press **Windows**, type `PowerShell`, and open it. A normal window — not "Run as administrator".

items.title: Install the package
items.text: Run `Add-AppxPackage`, giving it the path to the file. Adjust the path if you saved it somewhere other than Downloads.

blocks.text: Add-AppxPackage -Path "$HOME\Downloads\Mirall.msix"
Mirall appears in the Start menu when the command finishes. On success it prints nothing at all.
Why this happens

App Installer can fail while the part of Windows that actually installs packages is perfectly healthy. It updates through the Microsoft Store, so it goes stale on machines where Store or Windows Update traffic is blocked — and it deliberately turns down packages that declare certain restricted capabilities. Mirall declares one so it can keep your data at a real `%APPDATA%` path instead of inside a sandbox. The command above bypasses App Installer, so neither applies.
Machines with Windows updates deliberately frozen — by a blocking utility, on an LTSC image, air-gapped, or under a locked-down company policy — are the most likely to run into this.
If the command also fails
Unlike App Installer, it prints a real error code. These are the ones worth acting on:

rows: The signing certificate chain ends in a root this machine doesn't trust

Import the **Certum Trusted Network CA 2** root into Local Computer → Trusted Root Certification Authorities. Windows normally fetches it on demand, which fails on a machine that can't reach Windows Update.
You're in an elevated PowerShell window. Close it and use a normal one.

blocks.text: Still stuck? [install-windows.ps1](https://github.com/ok/mirall-app/blob/main/scripts/install-windows.ps1) in the Mirall repository collects what we need to diagnose it — Windows build, App Installer version, service states, the certificate chain as your machine sees it, and the last deployment events — and writes it to a text file. Download it, read it, then run it with `-Diagnose` and attach the file to your report.
You don't have to do anything — Mirall checks for new versions on its own and downloads them in the background. A staged update is applied the next time you quit and reopen Mirall, on your schedule.

When an update is waiting, a banner appears at the top of the window (you can dismiss it), and the pending version is also shown under **App** on your **Profile** page so you can always check what's coming.

reference.heading: Reference
reference.intro: Complete, lookup-able facts about Mirall — statuses, types, shortcuts, settings, and menus.

sections.title: File statuses
sections.intro: What each label on a file means. Colour carries meaning: green when a file is on your device, blue while it's moving, yellow when it needs your attention, red for an error, and grey when it's offered but not yet yours.

rows: A file you added to the space. It stays where it is on your disk and is offered to other members.
A file you downloaded from another member. It's yours to keep and works offline.
A transfer is in progress, showing progress, speed, and time remaining.
The download finished and Mirall is checking the contents match the owner's original.
The owner is still indexing this file. You can watch their progress while you wait.
A file you just added is being indexed so other members can fetch it.
A download stopped — because you paused it, or because it was interrupted. Resume to continue.
A transfer errored out. Retry to try again, or dismiss it.
The member who shared this file is online, so you can pull it. Click download.
The member who shared this file is offline. The download resumes on its own once they're back.
The file can't be obtained right now.

sections.title: The verified shield
sections.intro: A green shield next to a finished download means Mirall checked the file's contents against the owner's original and they match exactly. It appears only on a completed download, never on a file you shared yourself.

sections.title: Folder & share badges
sections.intro: The badge on a shared folder tells you your relationship to it.

rows: A folder on your computer that you share into the space. Your local changes sync to the space automatically.
A folder another member shares that you're looking through. Download individual files, or mirror the whole folder.
A folder another member shares that you keep as a live, read-only copy on your disk. It stays in sync as the owner changes it.
Work on this folder is held. Either a mirror whose syncing you've paused, or a folder you share whose adding you've paused. Nothing moves until you resume it.
A folder you share whose source folder has been moved or deleted. Point Mirall at its new location to reconnect it.

sections.title: The space sidebar
sections.intro: Each space view has a sidebar with a Drop to Share zone plus two panels — Space Storage and Members — that you can collapse to fold away what you're not using. The Members panel also switches between a row of avatars and the full list, with **Show all** and **Show less**. Each space remembers its own arrangement for as long as Mirall is running, so folding a panel away in one space leaves the others as you had them. Quitting Mirall returns every space to the default — both panels open, members as avatars.

image.alt: A Mirall space sidebar with the Space Storage panel collapsed and the Members panel expanded

sections.title: File & folder actions
list: **Download** — pull a file another member is offering onto your device.
**Reveal in Folder** — open a downloaded or shared file in your OS file browser.
**Unshare from Space** — remove a file you added so it's no longer offered (files others already downloaded stay on their devices).
**Browse Files** — look inside a shared folder without mirroring it.
**Open Folder** — open a folder you share, or a mirror, in your OS file browser.
**Delete Folder** — stop sharing a folder you own and remove it from the space.
**Locate folder…** — point Mirall at a shared folder that's missing on disk, after moving or reconnecting it.
**Pause Download** / **Resume** — stop a running download and continue it later from where it stopped.
**Cancel** — stop a running download outright and throw away what's been received.
**Discard Partial** — throw away a paused or stalled download and free the space it was using.
**Retry** / **Dismiss** — reattempt a download that ended in an error, or clear the failed row.
**Mirror to Disk…** — keep a live, read-only copy of a shared folder on your computer.
**Pause Mirror** / **Resume Mirror** — stop or restart a mirror's syncing.
**Change Mirror Location…** — move a mirror to a different folder.
**Unmount Mirror** — stop mirroring and remove the mirrored copy; the folder reverts to Browse.
**Free up space** — compact Mirall's own bookkeeping, in Settings → Storage.

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts
sections.intro: Press ⌘K / Ctrl-K to jump to any space or run any action; press ⌘/ / Ctrl-/ for this list inside the app. Anything without a chord of its own is in the command palette.

rows: Go back to the previous screen
Jump to a space by number — the first nine in your list
Join a space with an invite
Jump to the search box (Activity Log only)
Add files to the current space
Share a folder in the current space

sections.title: Getting around
sections.intro: Move through Mirall the way you would in a browser. Every screen can be reached from the keyboard — see [Get around with the keyboard](/docs/guides#use-the-keyboard).
list: **Back** — your mouse's back button, a two-finger swipe on macOS, `Cmd/Ctrl + ←`, or **View → Back**.
**Home** — click the Mirall logo, or press `Ctrl-H` (`Cmd-Shift-H` on macOS) to return to your Shared Spaces.
**A space by number** — `Cmd/Ctrl + 1` to `9` for the first nine spaces in your list, also listed by name under **View → Go to Space**.
**Command palette** — `Cmd/Ctrl + K` to search and jump to any space or run any action.
**Profile** and the **Activity Log** have chords of their own — `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P` and `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + L`.
**Network status**, the individual **Settings** pages, **What's new**, **Send feedback** and the documentation have no key of their own and are reached from the command palette.
**Invite to this space**, **Edit Space**, **Add to Favorites**, **Manage storage** and **Leave this space** are in the command palette while a space is open.

sections.title: Settings
sections.intro: The gear icon opens Settings — your preferences for the app itself. Your profile, this device, and the version you're running live separately on the Profile page (click your avatar).

rows: Background mode — “Show Mirall in the menu bar” on macOS, “Run in the background” on Windows and Linux — and Launch at login.
Theme Mode (Light / System / Dark), Display Size, Language, and — on Windows and Linux — auto-hide the menu bar.
Master switch, system sound, mute-when-focused, and five per-event toggles.
Transfer limits — a download and an upload cap, each Unlimited, a preset, or a figure you type.
Download folder — with a warning when Mirall can't reach it — and Mirall's own App Storage, a shared-file index plus the app database, with a Free up space action.
